text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Differing interests have slowed down the normalisation talks between Croatia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Out of 20 expected agreements only the consular convention was signed by the two foreign ministers on Tuesday.
- Tudjman is bound to win the first round of the presidential elections, says the head of his Croatian Democratic Union party's election headquarters, Ivic Pasalic.
- Croatia will become a member of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) on June 9.
- Deutsche Bank opens first Croatian office.

- Delegation from Eastern Slavonia headed by Serb representative Vojislav Stanimirovic and Transitional Administrator Jacques Klein invites president Tudjman to attend a session of the newly established local authorities in Beli Manastir.
- Friday's military parade, which marks Croatian Statehood Day, will be broadcast simultaneously via satellite and the internet. Some 2,000 spectators are expected.
- Tudjman, Zdravko Tomac and Vlado Gotovac are the three official candidates for June's presidential elections.

- Total budget revenues for the first quarter of 1997 have been put at 6.7 billion kuna, while total expenditures in the same period amount to 8 billion kuna. The difference is being made up by foreign loans.
- The pressures we are placing on Croatia mean we are taking you seriously, says Charles Redman, former U.S. envoy in the former Yugoslavia, in an interview.
- The INA oil company workers' trade union is threatening to stage a warning strike on June 12 if no progress is made in talks on a collective agreement.
- Commentary by economist M. Rakelic: Croatia lags behind its tourism competitors despite beautiful countryside and scenic villages.
- INA to introduce a credit card for payment at its filling stations this summer.
- Money market: Interest rates hold despite much weaker interbank demand. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
